newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices recover modestly.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices recover modestly.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices recovered modestly, assessed at from flat to down 1/8 of a point, following Treasuries, with much of the attention focused on New York City's big bond sale.

The city, one of the few municipal issuers capable of selling debt overseas, placed $300 million of bonds with European buyers, who paid a spread of 28 basis points over the three-month LIBOR, a rate that was at the low end of what New York City expected to have to pay in its second sale to Europe.

Domestic investors oversubscribed a tax-exempt offering, enabling the city to boost the size to $808 million from $550 million, and its yield of 6.32 percent for the top yield in 2025 matched analysts' forecasts.
"We hearing it went very well," a trader said. The city estimated that the refunding saved it $75 million.
However, a sale by New Jersey Wastewater did not appear to be as well-received, as there was a $51 million balance of $108.7 million of insured and uninsured refunding bonds that were sold.
Though only two of the four issues was insured, municipal analysts noted that the state did not seem to derive much benefit from enhancing its credit, as the scale was the same for all of the debt.
Traders said in part this reflected an unusually narrow spread between paper that is rated triple AAA and is insured and issues that are rated triple AA and are uninsured.
"More than anything else, it's the plethora of triple AAA volume, most everything comes insured and the lack of uninsured paper has condensed its spread," a trader said.
Two of the New Jersey issues won the rating agencies top rating, with two of them ranked one tier down at double AA.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Alliance Airport Authority Inc Texas Special Facilities Revenues of April 2021, which pay a 6-3/8 percent coupon, and were bid at 100-1/8, down from 99-7/8.
And Houston Texas Water & Sewer System Revenues of December 2022, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.76 percent NET, up two basis points.

The March municipal futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade ended at 114-29/32, down five ticks, with March Treasury bond futures closing at 111-9/32, down four ticks. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 26 ticks.
